name: Boosting Vaccine Uptake in LMICs Through HPSR

content.text: The workshop is part of a broader WHO-led programme launched to address persistent and emerging challenges around vaccine uptake in LMICs. These include policy gaps, systemic barriers, fluctuating public trust, and the need for evidence-based strategies that extend beyond individual behavioural factors. Recognising these complexities, six interdisciplinary research teams from Pakistan, India, Nigeria, Ethiopia, Indonesia, and the Philippines are exploring vaccine uptake through various lenses, community dynamics, health system structures, and national governance.

This marked the third meeting of these teams, following the initial "co-creation workshop" held in Geneva in February 2025. That meeting laid the foundation for a shared meta-narrative and a collaborative research framework. Building on that, this Karachi workshop offered a platform to share progress, provide technical support, and drive strategic communication approaches.

"Improving vaccine uptake is not just about changing individual behaviour, it requires understanding and reshaping the policies, systems, and structures that determine access and trust," said Dr Aku Kwamie, Acting Unit Head of Health Policy and Systems Research at WHO.

The sessions throughout the event were designed to provide both conceptual and practical value. These included country-specific presentations, discussions on behavioural science and evaluation methods, and deep dives into refining the shared meta-narrative. Teams also explored how to communicate their research findings more effectively to influence policy, moving beyond academic publications toward real-world change.

Two panel discussions spotlighted critical themes. The first tackled equity and innovation in immunization delivery, especially in resource-constrained settings. The second showcased Pakistan's success stories, featuring digital interventions, community-based approaches, and innovations in service delivery.

The workshop also held the launch of the REAPS-HS Collaborative Pakistan, a major new initiative aimed at boosting demand for health policy and systems research, and supporting evidence-informed policymaking in Pakistan.

The event had over 70% representation from research teams and senior faculty, including experts in maternal and child health, immunization, and digital health. The remaining 30% included research staff and early-career faculty, emphasizing the programme's commitment to capacity building and knowledge sharing across generations.

Ultimately, the workshop served not only to assess and refine ongoing research, but also to build stronger connections between countries and sectors, ensuring that systems-level insights can inform global and national immunisation strategies. The outcomes include updated country impact plans, a strengthened network of collaborators, and a clearer roadmap for translating research into practice.

content.title: Boosting Vaccine Uptake in LMICs Through HPSR
content.author: Faiza Hakim Shah
content.description: AKU's Department of Community Health Sciences hosted a significant workshop from 19-21 August 2025, focused on advancing health policy and systems research (HPSR) to improve vaccine uptake in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Organized by Dr. Zahid Ali Memon and his team, this annual learning workshop, held in collaboration with the Alliance for Health Policy and Systems Research, World Health Organization (WHO), brought together global and local researchers, policymakers, and health professionals to foster collaborative learning and strengthen immunisation systems.
